text: How information fits into the proposed enquiry and campaign process.
This page is a design and content draft. The legal operator, live data practices and final terms need confirmation before publication.

sections.name: Policy content
text: Enquiries ask for contact details and the information needed to understand your interest in a pilot. Creator enquiries may include a public profile link; brand enquiries may include a company and campaign idea.
The intended use is to reply to your enquiry, discuss pilot fit and arrange the next steps you agree to. Any other use needs clear notice.

A campaign may involve face or voice material, creator context, boundaries, licence terms and approval records. The collection and use of these materials must be explained before you take part. Signing up alone grants no likeness rights.

The published policy must identify the service providers that handle site enquiries and campaign materials. A campaign agreement should name the production tools and explain who may access its source material.
The published policy must state how long enquiry details, campaign files and approval records remain in storage, and how deletion requests work. These periods are still to be confirmed.

You can ask questions about the information you share, request a correction, or raise a privacy concern through Contact. Campaign permissions, expiry and renewal belong in the relevant campaign agreement.
The published policy must describe any analytics, cookies or similar tools the live site actually uses. The current design does not establish which tools will run on the site.
The final policy needs the legal operator’s name, a working privacy contact and an effective date. We will publish those details once the operating process is confirmed.

sections.name: Policy opening
text: The proposed ground rules for the site and pilot process.
This page is a design and content draft. The legal operator, live data practices and final terms need confirmation before publication.

sections.name: Policy content
text: Semblanse is developing a workspace for creator identity licensing and running initial campaigns hands-on. Public product screens and campaign figures illustrate the proposed experience.
Sending an enquiry expresses interest. Campaign participation depends on fit and a separate agreement. Share accurate contact and profile details so the team can reply.
Creating an enquiry or joining a list grants no rights to a person’s face or voice. Each campaign requires an agreed licence that defines the creator, brand, portrayal, channels, territory and term.

Creator context and stated boundaries guide the portrayal. The proposed process requires the creator to review each finished ad before it runs. Any new use or extension needs the permissions set out in the agreement.

Brands generally handle production with their chosen tools unless a managed pilot agrees otherwise. The campaign agreement needs to identify approved tools, access to source materials and any storage or deletion terms.
The parties agree scope, price and payment milestones for each campaign. Public sample fees do not set the price of a future campaign. The campaign agreement records the payment rules.
The campaign agreement should state when permission ends, how renewal works and what happens if the agreed use changes. Use Contact to raise a question or concern about an enquiry or pilot.
Before publication, confirm the legal operator, service terms, governing law, cancellation rules and dispute process. These draft site terms do not replace the separate campaign agreement.
